transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sara Kim (Evoke Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Ana Torres (Platform)

[00:00] Jordan Mills: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, i'm on the ae side. priya is our solutions engineer. how are you all?
[00:07] Sara Kim: good, thanks. excited to learn more. we've been poking at a few providers and wanted to figure out ttf - time to first token, and what it'd look like to start self-serve.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: yeah budget's tight, so we want to validate hosted api first. if performance looks good we may move to dedicated for prod.
[00:27] Priya Nair: cool, that's a common path. quick outline: we'll do a 30-ish minute discovery, then quick demo/quickstart pointers. we'll cover free credits, onboarding, security and dedicated migration options. any specific goals for today?
[00:38] Ana Torres: mostly infra questions — vpc options, data residency, kms, and how long before our devs can get tokens working.
[00:45] Jordan Mills: perfect. sara, can you share a bit about current stack? how are you calling models today?
[00:52] Sara Kim: we use a mix — internal API wrapping openai for chat features and an embeddings pipeline with cohere. we do batch embeddings nightly and real-time chat for product support. latency target for chat is sub 300ms p50, cost target is under $0.015 per 1k tokens ideally.
[01:12] Priya Nair: good context. our hosted API usually gets people up and running in minutes with SDK + quickstart. free credits can be provisioned for eval, and the quickstart repo has sample code for node/python. for latency, it depends on model choice and sequence length — we can get below 300ms for smaller context models on hosted with streaming off, or lower with tuned configs.
[01:33] Liam O'Connor: streaming off? we rely on streaming for UX. does that change latency much?
[01:38] Priya Nair: streaming affects perceived latency but also throughput; we support streaming and function-like calls. batching and KV cache can reduce cost significantly for repeated prefixes — useful for chat.
[01:48] Jordan Mills: also to call out: if you start hosted and then go Dedicated, we preserve API semantics and rollout policies so your app code doesn't need big changes.
[01:56] Sara Kim: nice. security — do you provide SOC 2 and SSO? we need SAML/Okta and audit logs for compliance.
[02:03] Jordan Mills: yes SOC 2 in the docs, SAML SSO + RBAC, audit logs are available. for private deployments there's VPC and on-prem, but that usually comes later. we'll share the security pack.
[02:13] Ana Torres: how are keys handled for hosted? can we rotate keys and use our KMS?
[02:18] Priya Nair: hosted API keys rotate, but for customer-managed keys you'd look at Private with KMS integrations or Dedicated with KMS. hosted supports encrypted at rest and in transit. we'll surface the key management options in the security doc.
[02:30] Liam O'Connor: what about data retention? we need to ensure no logging of PII for eval runs.
[02:35] Jordan Mills: we have data retention controls; hosted offers options to opt-out of data logging for enterprise accounts. Private or Dedicated gives you full control. we'll include exact retention windows in the doc.
[02:45] Sara Kim: on the PLG side, how does free credits work? can we get a sandbox for the team to test without a card?
[02:51] Jordan Mills: yes, self-serve sign-up gives free trial credits. for larger evals we can provision credit codes. Quickstart guides show time-to-first-token as minutes — clone repo, pip install, set API key, sample request.
[03:03] Priya Nair: we also have a hosted quickstart that takes about 10 minutes for devs to hit first token end-to-end if they follow the SDK quickstart. for a more realistic benchmark we usually provision ~100k tokens of credit.
[03:15] Ana Torres: that would be helpful. our devs prefer a short notebook.
[03:18] Jordan Mills: we'll send a notebook and a sample benchmark script.
[03:21] [04:00] (brief screen share mentioned, demo skipped on call)
[04:30] Priya Nair: about model selection — we have a catalog of curated open models and redwood-verified profiles. you can pin model versions for rollout, and we support quantized variants for cost savings.
[04:43] Sara Kim: can we run evals locally, like check latency on our infra before moving to dedicated?
[04:48] Priya Nair: yes, we can run small benchmark jobs from your VPC or share a perf harness. typically we do a bench with sample traffic patterns to recommend Dedicated GPU count and batching configs.
[04:59] Liam O'Connor: our target is 2k rps peak during business hours for embeddings and about 200 concurrent chat sessions. do you have rough numbers on Dedicated sizing?
[05:10] Priya Nair: rough ballpark yes — depends on model. we'll estimate in the follow-up. for hosted, we can handle spikes but guaranteed throughput is where Dedicated helps.
[05:22] Sara Kim: pricing? we need per-token hosted pricing and an idea of committed pricing for Dedicated.
[05:27] Jordan Mills: i'll send the tier sheet. hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is committed capacity with lower unit costs and burst options.
[05:34] Ana Torres: any networking constraints for private? we're a heavily firewalled environment.
[05:38] Priya Nair: Private supports customer-managed VPC connections and on-prem packages for air-gapped setups. we work with infra teams to map ports and proxy requirements.
[05:47] [06:15] (crosstalk)
[06:40] Sara Kim: talk to me about observability — how do we debug token costs per-route?
[06:45] Jordan Mills: the Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model. you can instrument tracing hooks and set regression alerts tied to eval prompts.
[06:55] Liam O'Connor: ok, sounds like a good fit conceptually. what's the typical timeline from signup to a small pilot?
[07:01] Priya Nair: for PLG quickstart, minutes to first token; for a pilot with SLA/Dedicated, usually 4-6 weeks including procurement.
[07:10] Jordan Mills: we also help with a small pilot plan and sample success criteria — p50 latency, token cost targets, and accuracy baselines.
[07:18] Sara Kim: any friction in onboarding devs? sdk maturity?
[07:22] Priya Nair: SDKs in node/python/go; examples for streaming and function-calling. devs usually onboard fast. occasional naming mismatches in auto transcriptions, but SDKs are stable.
[07:31] Ana Torres: about privacy — can we avoid sending logs during eval? we want to run sensitive prompts but not retain them.
[07:38] Jordan Mills: yes opt-out feature and for stricter needs, Private. We'll send the exact policy and steps in the security packet.
[07:46] [10:00] (discussion of internal stakeholders and procurement windows)
[10:30] Sara Kim: procurement — we're aiming to decide in 3 weeks. need security docs and a cost estimate to present.
[10:36] Jordan Mills: understood. we'll provide SOC2, network docs, and a pricing estimate.
[10:41] Priya Nair: i'll also run the perf estimate for your 2k rps target and share config suggestions.
[10:47] Liam O'Connor: can we get a short spike with free credits for the team to validate integration before procurement?
[10:52] Jordan Mills: yes. i'll generate a credit code and the quickstart notebook.
[10:56] Ana Torres: sample token distributions — sara will share that after the call.
[11:00] Jordan Mills: great. any other blockers?
[11:03] Sara Kim: timeline and compliance answers are blockers; also we want to understand how rollback to a smaller model works if regression occurs.
[11:11] Priya Nair: rollbacks are straightforward — you can pin previous model versions and we support canary rollouts with automatic fallback policies.
[11:18] Jordan Mills: recap: we'll send quickstart + credits, SOC2 and network doc, pricing sheet, and schedule a perf benchmark with priya. sara to share sample dataset.
[11:27] Sara Kim: sounds good. thanks.
[11:29] Liam O'Connor: thanks all.
[11:31] Jordan Mills: thanks, we'll follow up by tomorrow with assets.

(occasional transcription artifacts: "kv cahce" instead of kv cache, "redwood-verified" sometimes transcribed as "redwood verified", names occasionally glitched)

End of transcript.
